git_revision_note: The receipt ships with the commit it describes, so it cannot contain that commit's own identity. The branch freebuff/windows-test-performance-under-concurrent-load and its pull request carry it.
execution_mode: local desktop agent in one dedicated worktree on the shared laboratory VM; measurement commands run against this checkout only; no other campaign's worktree, branch or process was modified
model_note: Not exposed to agent tools. No paid provider was connected, no credits purchased, no additional AI worker launched, and no other campaign's agent was altered.

source.detail: Instrumented test runs and home-directory campaign registry written by this campaign's own harness.

coverage: One full portable suite execution under concurrent campaign load (727 tests, 2026-11-26 09:29-09:50 UTC), one controlled two-arm fixture comparison on a single module, and one full portable suite execution in a lower-contention window (in progress at checkpoint time). Host conditions recorded by the harness for each run.
attribution_limits: Host CPU, memory, process and thread counts describe a shared VM and are not provider consumption. Suite wall-clock is test execution time, not agent session time. No per-campaign or account-level provider allowance is observable to the agent.
status: checkpoint: concurrent-load baseline recovered and analysed; harness sys.path defect corrected; synthetic task fixture reuse measured; test-synchronization finding handed to the branch that already fixes it
measurement_note: Provider allowance, tokens, context size and quota remain unobservable to the agent; no figure is estimated or inferred from a shared account meter. measured_test_wall_clock sums instrumented test execution only and excludes agent session time: 1284.3 s for the full baseline plus 45.8 s across the smoke run and the two-arm fixture comparison. The second full run was still executing at checkpoint time and is not included. Campaign activity counts are reported as activity, not as provider consumption.
private_evidence: Raw run JSON, host timelines, logs and the campaign registry are retained outside Git under the laboratory private-evidence directory; only the harness, the analysis and this reviewed receipt are published.
